MosoFin skill · recurring-transaction-builder · learning guide

From one rent bill to a schedule that keeps running

This page shows how the skill designs, checks and audits a recurring schedule, one level at a time. It starts with one rent bill on one date. It ends with the monthly check that each bill actually ran. The page quotes every rule from the skill and works every number in front of you.

The rules are the skill's ownThe page quotes each rule word for word, with the file and section it comes from.
Outside sources back the factsThey are a US holiday list, an OpenStax textbook, a GAO audit guide, the FASB lease standard and a BLS page. Each one has a number and a link.
The page shows the mathOpen "Check it yourself" on any level. Follow every line on a calculator.
Your numbers, your checkAt the end, enter your own amount, dates and increase. The page builds every row and the total.
Rule: quoted from the skill Fact: from a cited authority, numbered like 1 Example: made-up figures, calculated in full
How it thinks

Eight rules the whole skill runs on

Every level below applies one or more of these rules. The examples use one made-up company, Northbrook Trading, which keeps its books in US dollars on the accrual basis, with a calendar year. The run date is Thursday 29 October 2026. The skill designs the schedule and checks it. It never creates the template, never posts and never schedules anything. A person enters the specification.

Learning path

Six levels, from simple to complex

Check it yourself

Build a recurring schedule

Enter an amount, a start date and the rules, or load an example. The page runs the date and amount part of Steps 3 and 4 from references/method.md. It does not check your books. The page sends nothing anywhere.

The schedule
The day rule and the roll

Saturdays and Sundays are always non-business days here. The holiday switch adds the US federal holiday dates for 2027 and 2028 only, on the date itself and not on the observed day. The page rounds each new amount to the cent at each anniversary of the start date, and the increase compounds. A day that a month does not have rolls to the last day of that month. If a business-day roll would leave the month, the page rolls the other way for that row. The memo says so. Step 3 does this for period-end entries. The Northbrook preset gives 7 rolls and a total of $207,060.00. We made up the second preset. It gives 12 rows and a total of $1,440.00, with no row skipped.

Using it

What it asks, needs and gives back

Asks firstUse MosoFin for this run, or upload the data? What type, and with which vendor or customer? What amount and currency? Which start date, and which end date or count? Which cadence and day rule? Which coding and tax code? Which payment terms? Which holiday calendar and roll policy? Which escalation and stop terms? How to treat a partial first or last period?
NeedsThe skill needs the schedule's terms from you, because they are in the contract. To check your books, it reads the chart of accounts, the vendor or customer list and the tax codes. It also reads the list of recurring templates and up to 24 months of history.
Gives backThe skill gives back a specification in six sheets: summary, occurrences, posting detail, reversals for accruals, validation and discovery, and coverage. Every row is Pending, under a NOT POSTED header. It asks before it makes an Excel file.
NeverThe skill never creates the template, posts an occurrence or schedules anything. It never says "posted", "created" or "scheduled". It never picks a holiday calendar or a rate for you. It never builds a schedule before it checks for one that already exists.
Sources

Where every fact on this page comes from

The rules are the skill's own. The facts below come from five outside sources. They are a US holiday list, an OpenStax textbook, a GAO audit guide, the FASB lease standard and a BLS page. MosoFin checked each one on 28 October 2026 from search results and did not open the pages. Follow the link for today's wording.

    Not backed by an outside authority. The six stages, the Pending status, the NOT POSTED header and the six sheets are the skill's own. So are the 12- or 24-month horizon, the duplicate check and the run audit. MosoFin made up Northbrook Trading, its suppliers and every figure in the examples. The $8,500 rent comes from the skill's own read-back example. All five sources are US sources. Other countries have their own lease standards, holiday calendars and price indexes.
